dispatch_rule: Exact source/context hashes and ownership must verify; independent packet review and separate explicit root dispatch approval required. Prepared packet is not execution authority.
objective: Add a private derived index for currently preempting queued/suspended waiters so production victim replacement can select the first eligible waiter without globally projecting/sorting all waiters. Preserve existing scheduling semantics and failure atomicity.
scope: Private Flow/ECS implementation, tests, benchmark-label correction, and owned evidence only. No public API, serialization/checkpoint format, generic queue redesign, dependency change, unrelated lifecycle refactor, or acceptance-gate change. The full 100k Flow case remains a blocker until actual integrated behavior is measured and accepted.

proposed_private_component.name: PreemptingWaiters
proposed_private_component.placement: Private ECS component attached to each resource entity at creation; removed with the resource.
proposed_private_component.membership: Exactly requests in Queued or Suspended state for that resource whose can_preempt is true. Pending/active requests are absent. PriorityKey ordering is the existing (priority_level, original_admission_sequence, request_id) ordering.
proposed_private_component.witness: Validate expected_len == keys.len() and keys.len() <= primary waiting-queue len when staging a resource. This is a cardinality witness, not a claim to detect every untouched equal-cardinality corruption.
proposed_private_component.cache_validation: Before using the first cached key, validate its request exists, names the resource, is Queued or Suspended, can_preempt is true, has the exact indexed PriorityKey, and is present in the primary waiting queue. Missing component for a registered resource is InvalidState before authoritative mutation. Preserve deadline-index validation/preflight as a paired derived-cache contract.
proposed_private_component.creation_removal: Create empty component with resource; remove component with resource. Do not change public or serialized state.

centralized_membership_transitions: Successful Submit directly into queued waiting state with can_preempt=true: insert exact key.

Timeout, cancellation, despawn, or grant/removal from waiting queue: remove exact old key before changing/removing its indexed state; grant clears/removes waiting deadline/index as already contracted.
Queued reprioritization: remove old key, then insert new key preserving original admission sequence.

Victim remains absent from cache while Active. After Suspend/Restart requeues as Suspended, insert resulting exact key iff can_preempt=true. Abort never requeues/adds. Do not remove an active victim key that never existed.
Restart/requeue: insert iff resulting state is Queued or Suspended and can_preempt=true.
Abort/no-requeue and active rekey: do not add to waiting preemption index.
replacement_algorithm: When primary queue has free capacity, retain existing ordinary grant selection/order; maintain both private indexes before state changes.

When full, read minimum PreemptingWaiters key. If empty, stop BEFORE constructing/projecting any holder candidates. For Some key validate request exists, resource matches, state Queued|Suspended, can_preempt=true, exact PriorityKey and primary queue membership; failures return InvalidState before authoritative mutation.

After validated first key, construct holders using existing allocation ordering and holder eligibility rules. Supply std::iter::once(validated WaitingCandidate) to production ordered helper. Cache minimum is legacy sort first preemption-capable waiter; if it cannot strictly outrank globally worst eligible holder, no later cached key can qualify. Keep worst-holder priority/admission/ID comparator unchanged.
Promote ordered helper to production. Keep old sorting selector and select_victim as cfg(test) independent references. No materialization/sorting of all waiting requests in Flow.
failure_atomicity: All fallible cache, request, resource, queue, and capacity validation must finish for the full affected causal closure/group before authoritative mutation or event-head advancement. Any corrupt cache/key/queue returns InvalidState with authoritative state and externally visible head unchanged. Preserve current deadline paired-index preflight and group atomicity; do not turn derived-cache failure into partial queue/request/resource changes.
tests: Unit test empty and populated index ordering; duplicate insert/remove behavior follows explicit invariants and cannot silently desynchronize expected_len.

Lifecycle table for create/remove resource; submit queued; pending-to-queued; queued reprioritize; queued cancel/despawn/timeout; grant; queued-to-suspended victim; restart/requeue; abort; active rekey. Verify exact membership and expected_len after each transition.

Differential deterministic grids against the old sorting selector: priority ties/extremes, admission-sequence/request-ID tie order, holder ties and permutations, can_preempt false, no eligible holders, no waiters, queued and suspended holders/waiters, due/equal/missing completion boundaries.

Prove empty-cache branch avoids holder projection using a directly tested private lazy closure helper if introduced, or a fixture with poisoned holder projection data plus empty cache that completes without evaluating it; avoid fabricated counters derived from formulas. Pure ordered helper no-eligible-holder iterator nonconsumption oracle remains.

Corruption matrix: missing component, wrong expected_len, oversized cache, first key missing request, wrong resource/state/can_preempt/key, absent primary queue membership, malformed paired deadline key. Each must fail InvalidState before commit/head change.

Multi-resource causal group failure where a later resource/key is corrupt after earlier resource work is staged; assert all authoritative resources, requests, queues, deadline/preemption indexes, and event head remain unchanged.
Active lease behavior: active request is never indexed; reprioritizing an active lease leaves lease/queue semantics unchanged and does not create membership.

requirements: After caller switch, old sorting-selector and select_victim rows become explicitly historical_sorting_reference/historical_victim_reference. Current ordered-helper rows become production_ordered_selector_kernel, still kernel-only and excluding index maintenance/holder projection. Do not label raw ordered-helper timing as complete indexed Flow path; full runtime matrix supplies that evidence.
Retain ordered-selector kernel rows as kernel-only diagnostics; do not present them as Flow end-to-end evidence.
Do not alter canonical Criterion harness, accepted baseline, threshold source, or claim speedup until the integrated full workload and baseline/current comparison run are complete.
